newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST -- Gasoline build seen again in API data.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST -- Gasoline build seen again in API data.

text.p: REUTER SURVEY ESTIMATES* ACTUAL STOCKS FOR
*NB - The survey estimate is derived by omitting the high and low forecast and averaging the rest, with a sample of at least six.

Tuesday night's oil inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) is expected by dealers to show a build in gasoline stocks for the fourth consecutive week with refined product output continuing at a torrid pace.
But, dealers were divided as to whether this would be one of the last builds of the season after record output has created ample supply.

"The most significant thing about the report will be gasoline. This could be one of the last builds before we start to see seasonal declines," said Bill O'Grady, analyst with A.G. Edwards in St. Louis.

"I think it is unlikely that this will be one of the last builds given refineries are producing around 8.0 million barrel a day (of gasoline)," John Saucer, analyst with Smith Barney in Houston, adding the real key of the report is the refined product output itself.
Dealers expect refinery utilization to decline 0.5 percentage point after rising 0.7 percentage point to 97.6 percent for the week ended June 13. Tonight's data reflects the week ended June 20.
Refinery rates have reflected breakneck gasoline output which reached a record 8.23 million barrels per day (bpd) the week before last.

In recent reports, implied demand has been a strong eight million bpd plus, but dealers still expect a gasoline stock build of up to one million barrels in tonight's data since output was expected to outstrip demand just as it has in weeks previous.
Although crude run rates are expected to have moderated from a 15.1 million bpd, they have been at such a high rate that crude runs are still able to offset somewhat hefty crude imports.

"Another increase is anticipated in crude stocks due partially to a continued strong import pace in the 8.5 million bpd area," said Jim Ritterbusch, a trader with Sweeney Oil in Chicago. Dealers are expecting crude stocks to build up to one million barrels. For the June 13 week, crude imports in the API report hit a record 9.2 million bpd.
Distillate stocks, comprised of heating oil and diesel, were once again supposed to rise about two to three million barrels with heating oil out of season amid high refinery runs.
